title: Canada-resident NRI trapped using a fake ID, demand of 50 thousand dollars, Ghaziabad police's big action against a sextortion gang

reading.body:
This is a case of alleged criminal extortion in which AI-generated video was one tool among several, not a failure of a deployed AI system. The reported use of AI was to produce obscene videos of a person, alongside a fake social media profile and a recorded call, as leverage in a blackmail scheme. Nothing in the reporting describes a model or product behaving incorrectly, so the incident does not show a model asserting false facts, a system deployed without human review, or a system used outside its intended conditions.

The point in the scheme where the AI material was used was the threat stage, after contact had been made and a compromising recording obtained. The reported demand was for money, with the videos named as the means of pressure if the victim did not comply. Catching this kind of conduct does not turn on model safeguards, because the harm lies in the surrounding deception and coercion rather than in any single generated output.

What is established is that police registered a case, made arrests, and linked a phone number to prior complaints. What is not established is guilt, since an arrest and a registered FIR are not findings of a court, and the reported scale of the operation rests on police statements rather than on adjudicated facts.

summary:
A Jamia Millia Islamia student named Md Faisal, 22, and three associates from Muzaffarnagar were arrested in Ghaziabad for allegedly extorting a Canada-based NRI. Police said the gang created a fake Facebook profile, recorded the victim in a compromising position during a Sept 10 video call, then demanded $50,000 while threatening to circulate the footage and AI-generated obscene videos. The victim contacted the cybercrime team on Sept 17, and the accused's mobile number was linked to 40 cyber fraud complaints.

Police registered an FIR under the BNS and IT Act and arrested four gang members on Friday, while some accomplices remain absconding. Investigators said the gang had been active since 2023, cheated hundreds of people in India and abroad, and used mule accounts and AI sextortion videos. Their phones revealed links to at least 130 bank accounts holding Rs 6.6 crore.
